Change c0253. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XIII.

Context before (unchanged): Through this work I obtained a cursory knowledge of history, and a view of the several empires at present existing in the world; it gave me an insight into the manners, governments, and religions of the different nations of the earth.

1818 text: I heard of the slothful Asiatics; of the stupendous genius and mental activity of the Grecians; of the wars and wonderful virtue of the early Romans—of their subsequent degeneration—of the decline of that mighty empire; of chivalry, Christianity, and kings.

1831 text: I heard of the slothful Asiatics; of the stupendous genius and mental activity of the Grecians; of the wars and wonderful virtue of the early Romans—of their subsequent degenerating—of the decline of that mighty empire; of chivalry, Christianity, and kings.

Diff: I heard of the slothful Asiatics; of the stupendous genius and mental activity of the Grecians; of the wars and wonderful virtue of the early Romans—of their subsequent [-degeneration-] {+degenerating+} —of the decline of that mighty empire; of chivalry, Christianity, and kings.

Context after (unchanged): I heard of the discovery of the American hemisphere, and wept with Safie over the hapless fate of its original inhabitants.

result.rationale: Noun 'degeneration' becomes participle 'degenerating' in 'of their subsequent degenerating'; same meaning of decline, a grammatical/diction swap with no change to events or moral judgment.
